headline: Anthropic's IPO filing revives the AI trade; chips jump ~3% and Nasdaq +0.8% as oil eases
summary: A tech-led rebound that faded from its highs. Stocks opened higher as oil slipped, then climbed through the morning once Anthropic's S-1 hit, with the S&P 500 up about 0.9% and the Nasdaq about 1.2% by late morning before both gave back part of the gain into the close. Tech (+1.7%) and industrials (+1.4%) led while communication services fell 1.6%; breadth stayed thin, with new 52-week lows still outnumbering new highs.
drivers: Anthropic S-1 lifts AI and chips

Anthropic's public IPO filing showed $16.3 billion of first-half revenue and hundreds of billions of dollars of multi-year compute commitments with SpaceX, Microsoft, Amazon, Google and others, easing worries about AI demand. The SOX rose about 3% after a steep October slide: Nvidia gained about 2.5% and led the S&P 500, Micron about 3%, Arm 6.3%, and optical names Lumentum (+8.2%), Applied Optoelectronics (+7.3%) and Coherent (+5.9%) topped the gainers.
Oil steps back from six-month highs

Hopes of mediation between the US and Iran cut WTI 1.5% to $101.76 and December Brent 0.9% to $110.74, despite continued Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. Treasury yields were little changed before the Fed: the 10-year slipped to about 4.98% and the 2-year edged up to 4.71% after a slightly soft $69 billion auction.

Meta fell 1.3% after laying out plans to raise up to $95 billion in equity for AI spending, and Verizon lost 3.7% on a revenue miss, dragging communication services. Neoclouds swung after Elon Musk warned debt markets were shutting out AI-only compute renters: CoreWeave dropped 5.5% early before ending up 3.6%.

Tesla jumped 5.2% to a three-month high after a Barclays upgrade to overweight. Brazil's Bovespa sank 14.7% after President Lula's surprise reelection raised fiscal worries, pulling down US-listed Petrobras (−14% to −16%) and MercadoLibre (−8%).
week: Monday alone more than erased the S&P 500's 0.5% loss of last week, leaving it about 1.8% below its early-October record; the backdrop remains a 10-year yield near 5% (off a 24-year high of 5.37% on Oct 7), oil above $100 and a Fed that hiked to 4% in September.
watch: Next: the Fed decides Wednesday Oct 28 (a hold is widely expected; Chair Warsh's tone on further hikes is the focus), with Alphabet, Microsoft and SK hynix reporting the same day, Amazon, Intel and Samsung on Thursday alongside GDP and inflation data, and the Nov 3 midterms after that.
